checks.claim: domain/full accepted input
checks.reason: Actual full balanced marked tilings, D>=2 and positive integer p; one fixed admissible J, one valid cut and common c across family. Official varying-n rates are not claimed.

checks.claim: OC homeomorphism and degeneracies
checks.reason: Read full exact accepted OC1–OC3. Finite positive physical tile determinants yield full inverse and uniform bilipschitz maps, while weighted Cauchy–Binet bounds A inverse for bounded J even at zero tangent minors.

checks.claim: CW0 signed translation
checks.reason: Reconstructed V′S=V and V′(p sigma)=-b0. Then c′=J′b0+Sc+p sigma lies in ker V′ and b=WSc+pW sigma; F uses original x with no doubled translation.

checks.claim: CW0 common target offset and error
checks.reason: Direct substitution gives c*=c′-J*Wc′ in ker W and a′-J*F-c*=(I-J*W)Se. S is orthogonal, so delta=||W||E after fixed-D norm conversion. All family constants are common.

checks.claim: CW1 winding core inclusion
checks.reason: For y in P with boundary distance >delta, every point of the straight boundary homotopy stays away from y. Winding remains one and the full homeomorphism identifies F(int Q). This uses degree, not Hausdorff alone.

checks.claim: CW1 whole buffer, empty cores and inverse bound
checks.reason: A closed erosion at margin t>delta includes its boundary by the same positive-distance argument. Whole required neighborhood is an explicit subset hypothesis. Large E may leave no core. CW1′ follows by applying A inverse to the displacement.

checks.claim: CW2 whole-tile image coverage
checks.reason: A source tile meeting Q0 lies wholly within its d_tile neighborhood; the error and margin put the entire actual image tile in Pplus. Extra recorded tiles outside controlled Q need no local error estimate for their exact inverse.

checks.claim: CW2 connected graph and one anchor
checks.reason: The connected convex Pplus is covered by its intersecting tiles, so their union and tile-edge graph are connected, including vertex-only contacts. A spanning tree plus one canonical height anchor integrates all colored increments.

checks.claim: CW2 anchor range and known location
checks.reason: Choose anchor vertex deterministically from target geometry. Its D integer heights lie in [0,p], hence at most (p+1)^D possibilities. Keep O_D(log(R+2)) with R>=max(2,p); no assumption p or R is O(window size).

checks.claim: CW2 exact recovery and representative injection
checks.reason: Recover each source vertex using x′=V′a′, reverse signs/permutation, and add b0. Filter reconstructed whole tiles by Q0. Select one full extension per source restriction before mapping; equal target record plus anchor forces equal source restriction.

checks.claim: CW3 reference Jordan disk and complete gluing
checks.reason: Closed Jordan union Omega inside F(int Q) has an actual whole-tile Jordan inverse C. Same complete target boundary makes any filling glue to the unchanged actual full target exterior.

checks.claim: CW3 unchanged exterior canonical lift
checks.reason: Omega is strictly inside full target polygon, so its exterior is connected. Original outer normalization and identical colored edges fix identical lift there, including Omega boundary; exact full inverse fixes original fine exterior and boundary.

checks.claim: CW3 old boundary versus new interior inverse
checks.reason: The new full inverse maps Omega to the bounded Jordan disk with exactly the old boundary partial C. Its interior point map may change. Forward bijection recovers target choices; no new interior affine estimate is assumed.

checks.claim: CW4 exact grid lift for all integers
checks.reason: On each enlarged reference tile the unit M-grid has affine lift a_MT(Mx)=M a_T(x), consistently across shared edges and normalization, for every positive integer M.

checks.claim: CW4 map and reference region commutation
checks.reason: Using Mp and Mb0 gives F_MT(Mx)=M F_T(x). The target reference is exactly subdivided, so M Omega pulls back to exactly M C; CW3 applies to this single dilated original reference.

checks.claim: CW4 complete consecutive rank ports
checks.reason: Each original rank interval [r-1,r] dilates to M unit consecutive ranks. Flipped ranks s->Mp-s+1 reverse precisely that block. No new matching or permutation is chosen.

checks.claim: CW4 disjoint source regions from one reference
checks.reason: C_alpha lies strictly inside its own Q_alpha. Disjoint window interiors therefore give disjoint closed fine patches at every scale, all obtained from one actual reference T.

checks.claim: CW4 product gluing and local recovery
checks.reason: Each chart supplies a filling of its fixed fine boundary. Glue disjoint patches to one exterior; restrict final tiling and apply each local forward chart with inherited boundary lift to recover the tuple. Global maps need not commute.

checks.claim: boundary and counterexample attempts
checks.reason: Tried missing signs, vanished minors, empty erosion, thin image, vertex-only source/target contact, unbounded p, nonunique extensions, changing inverse, all M and incompatible global charts. Explicit hypotheses/formulas dispose of each; no substantive counterexample found.

checks.claim: scope and dependency firewall
checks.reason: No canonical image equality, free margins, global reference from separate code classes, dropped log R, entropy/H/PR/UR4/global recovery or official rate. No DG/CUT/ST/RM/LW/US conclusion is a premise.
